description: Labelled decomposition cases. For each task we assert which app(s) MUST be chosen, which MUST NOT be, and a sensible subtask-count range. Routing is model-driven, so bounds are deliberately loose — the point is to catch clear misroutes and over/under-decomposition, not to pin exact prose.

cases.task: Explain how self-attention works in transformers.
cases.note: LLM/transformer topic -> the CME 295 specialist, not the generic Teach Me app (the collision that caused the live failure).

cases.task: Help me understand p-values and hypothesis testing.
cases.note: Statistics -> the stats tutor, not the generic learner.

cases.task: Teach me the basics of photosynthesis from first principles.
cases.note: General non-LLM/non-stats topic -> Teach Me is correct here.

cases.task: Find recent papers on mixture-of-experts and summarize the key takeaways.
Run Python code to compute the first 20 Fibonacci numbers and show the output.
cases.note: Code execution -> Simulated Learning; Coding Playground has no REST execute (WS-only).

cases.task: Give me a summary of this week's AI news.
cases.note: Curated AI news -> Intelligence Deck, not social aggregation.

cases.task: What is trending on Twitter about AI right now?
cases.note: Twitter/X trends -> Social Media AI, not the news deck.

cases.task: Ingest the LangChain GitHub repository and extract its key patterns.
cases.note: Repo ingestion + pattern extraction -> Github Learnings.

cases.task: Draft a blog post about agentic AI in my voice.
cases.note: Personal blog drafting -> Blogs Playground, not the research report tool.

cases.task: Do a deep research report on retrieval-augmented generation with citations.
cases.note: Long-form cited research -> Research Assistant, not blog drafting.

cases.task: What was the final score of the 2022 FIFA World Cup final?
Preview the first rows of the Titanic dataset.
cases.note: Dataset browse/preview -> Coding Playground's dataset ops.

cases.task: Explain how LLM pre-training works, teach me the intuition, show runnable code that demonstrates it, and write a blog post about it.
cases.note: The live failure case: distinct asks (explain / code / blog) must each become a subtask on the right specialist.

cases.task: Summarize this week's AI news and also find recent arXiv papers on diffusion models.
cases.note: Two unrelated asks -> two subtasks on two apps.

cases.task: Explain gradient descent and show me runnable Python that demonstrates it.
cases.note: Explanation + runnable code -> at least a code step on Simulated Learning; explanation may share the app.
A single simple ask should stay small (guards against over-decomposition).

cases.task: Create graphs and charts illustrating CLT concepts
cases.note: Graph/chart work needs a plotting library. Simulated Learning's sandbox has none; Coding Playground's kernel renders matplotlib. This is the live CLT-graphs failure of 2026-08-04.
